$comment: Every rendered verdict on this page carries a data-verdict marker, and every marker listed here has been forced false and watched go red. A mutation counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the same run, the failure was that marker's OWN assertion, and the run served the mutated bundle (CI=1, port 4684, no reused server). e2e/verdicts.spec.ts fails on any rendered marker missing from this file. Every branch that writes a marker has its own mutation: markers with more than one code path carry more than one entry, because covering the marker is not the same as covering the branch.

dleq.renders: #dleq — whether the client accepted the issuer's DLEQ proof under the key it was told to trust

mutations.kills: e2e/claims.spec.ts:55 expect(getByText('DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED')).toBeVisible()
mutations.observed: baseline cc92c383e9cce4e1773ad92efbc7a2f8 15 passed; mutated 24188700e77fb6978d541f39da7a564f 1 failed / 14 passed. Verbatim: "Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByText('DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED') / Expected: visible / Error: element(s) not found" at claims.spec.ts:55. The unpublished-key mode stopped aborting and rendered 'DLEQ PROOF · ACCEPTED AN UNPUBLISHED KEY' instead.

mutations.mutation: hand Alice `{ verifyKey: bobIssuer.publicKey }` so the key she was told to trust is not the key that answered her
mutations.observed: baseline cc92c383e9cce4e1773ad92efbc7a2f8 15 passed; mutated 33a27c733002186d3cdfa8f86e05c684 2 failed / 13 passed. Verbatim: "Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByText('DLEQ PROOFS · BOTH VERIFIED') / Expected: visible / Error: element(s) not found" at claims.spec.ts:42. The second failure is collateral, not a second finding: e2e/a11y.spec.ts:31 walks the partition fixture and clicks '2. Redeem at origin' unconditionally, and the abort leaves that button disabled, so it times out. M1 could not reach this path -- it forces DLEQ verification to accept, which leaves 'BOTH VERIFIED' standing.
